title: Customer Optimization Advisory: Priority Decision Framework for Enterprise Requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Create a repeatable decision framework and intake workflow that lets PMs and Solutions Engineering quickly triage non-bug optimization requests from enterprise customers (batching / caching knobs, quantization profiles, routing policies). The framework should balance time-to-value for customers, engineering effort, and SLA commitments for Dedicated/Private customers.

Scope:
- Intake form and metadata schema for advisory requests (customer tier, expected QPS, latency SLO, data sensitivity, SLA required, urgency, business impact).
- Scoring rubric to prioritize requests across: cost-savings potential, reliability risk, security/compliance impact, engineering complexity, and number of impacted customers.
- Triage pathways: quick-advice (Solutions Eng playbook), pilot project (Dedicated customer with reserved capacity + runtime support), and engineering project (feature work tracked by ENG).
- Prescriptive recommendations per request type: safe defaults for batching/caching knobs, recommended quantization profiles for common model families, routing policy templates (latency-first, cost-first, hybrid).
- Handoff artifacts: templated runbook, required telemetry dashboards, expected rollback criteria, and test prompt set for quality regression checks.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Intake form built in Zendesk/Confluence with required fields and computed priority score.
2) Scoring rubric documented and agreed by Runtime leads and Solutions Eng; rubric includes numeric weights and example worked cases.
3) Three routing policy templates documented with recommended telemetry metrics and an example rollout plan.
4) Playbook for quick-advice responses with standard phrasing and links to console settings.
5) Pilot plan template for engineering-backed changes including telemetry dashboards and QA prompts.
6) RACI established for triage steps (PM triage, Solutions Eng execution, ENG for code changes).

Out-of-scope: automated customer-facing recommendations within Console (that is phase 2). Full automation of kernel/quantization selection is also out-of-scope for this ticket.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Human-in-the-loop scoring enables nuanced judgment for enterprise requests but adds latency to response times; we'll provide an SLA target for 'quick-advice' responses (48 business hours) rather than realtime.
- Conservative quantization guidance reduces regression risk but may under-deliver cost savings for some private deployments; recommend experiments for high-value customers.
- Integration surface: prefer lightweight intake (Zendesk + Google Sheet) initially to iterate quickly; long term move into Console intake and automation.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Week 1 (Mar 1–Mar 7): Draft intake form and scoring rubric; align with Runtime and Solutions Eng.
- Week 2 (Mar 8–Mar 14): Finalize playbooks and routing policy templates; create Confluence home page.
- Week 3 (Mar 15–Mar 21): Pilot with 2 enterprise customers (identify volunteers via CSM); refine rubric based on cases.
- Week 4 (Mar 22–Mar 28): Hand off to ENG for any feature work and document post-mortem.

Telemetry and success metrics:
- Time-to-first-response for advisory requests (target: <=48 business hours for quick-advice).
- Percent of advisory requests resolved without engineering code changes (target: >=60% after pilot).
- Median customer-reported satisfaction score for advisory interactions (target: >=4/5).
- Number of regressed prompt cases detected during pilot (target: 0 critical regressions).
